                                     JUDGMENT

1. Accused persons Dev Sharma @ Monu, Sonu Sharma, Beerawati and Sonia faced trial for offences, punishable u/s 498A/304B/34 IPC.

2. Prosecution story, as per chargesheet is that on, 18.12.2014, an information regarding a lady committing suicide by hanging was received vide DD no.47A at around 8:10 pm, pursuant to which SI B.D. Meena alongwith Ct. Ram Avtar reached at H.No.D-1305, First Floor, Tajpur Pahari, Badarpur, Delhi, where they found one lady was hanging on ceiling fan. On inquiry, name of said lady was found to be Sonam W/o Deveshwar Sharma @ Monu aged 23 years. Since, death of said lady had taken place within 7 years of her marriage so, SDM and Executive Magistrate concerned were informed. The concerned Executive Magistrate had informed about the death of deceased Sonam to her family members. Crime Team was also called and Crime Team conducted the inspection at the spot and photographs of crime scene were taken. The dead body of deceased was sent to AIIMS Mortuary for preservation. During the course of investigation, the parents of deceased appeared before the Executive Magistrate, who recorded their statements. Dead body of deceased was identified by her parents and postmortem of the dead body was conducted. FIR No.744/2014 State Vs. Dev Sharma @ Monu & Ors. PS Badarpur Page No. 2 of 48 Exhibits were secured and dead body was then handed over to the family members. During the course of investigation statement of witnesses U/s 161 Cr.P.C. was recorded. Further, during the course of investigation, accused persons were arrested, their personal search were conducted and their disclosure statement were also recorded.

3. In the statement, Sh. Sunil Kumar (father of deceased Sonam) stated that his daughter deceased Sonam was performed court marriage with Dev Sharma @ Monu S/o Sh. Hari Om R/o H.No. D-1305, Near Barat Ghar, Tajpur Phari, Badarpur, New Delhi in the month of January, 2011. However, none of the family members from the side attended the marriage of his daughter with accused Dev Sharma @ Monu. He alongwith his family around three years earlier used to reside in Budh Vihar, Tajpur Pahadi, Badarpur, Delhi, and thereafter, they started residing in his native village. Accused Dev Sharma @ Monu was working as Master Roll in DTC and residing at D-1305, Near Barat Ghar, Tajpur Phari, Badarpur, New Delhi. Father of the deceased Sunil Kumar used to meet with his deceased daughter Sonam after her marriage and during their meeting her daughter used to enquire about his land and he used to tell that decision of his land likely to come soon and on this his deceased daughter Sonam requested him thrice for Rs.10,00,000/-. Deceased Sonam and his husband were having a dispute. On 18.12.2014 at about 9 pm his son was informed by someone that his daughter Sonam committed suicide by hanging herself and he immediately rushed to the house of his daughter at Delhi around 11:30 pm but the house was found locked. Thereafter, he went to PS Badarpur and gave a complaint against the jeth, jethani, saas, husband of deceased Sonam regarding beating, torturing and FIR No.744/2014 State Vs. Dev Sharma @ Monu & Ors. PS Badarpur Page No. 3 of 48 harassing his deceased daughter on account of non fulfillment of their illegal demand of Rs.10,00,000/-. Based on said statement, FIR in question was registered and investigation ensued.

4. On the aforesaid statement of Sh. Sunil Kumar father of deceased Sonam on 19.12.2024, FIR was registered on 19.12.2014, U/s 498A/304B/34 of the Indian Penal Code.

5. After filing of the chargesheet, Court took cognizance of the offences against accused. Proceedings under Section 207 Cr.P.C were concluded.

6. Arguments on charge were heard and based on the contents of chargesheet, accused persons was charged with offences punishable under Section 498A/304B/34 IPC on 19.05.2023 to which they pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. Matter was then fixed for prosecution evidence.

9. Prosecution witnesses deposed regarding the offence in the present matter as follows:

PW-1 Sh. Sunil Kumar (complainant/father of the deceased) deposed that his deceased daughter Sonam got married to accused Dev FIR No.744/2014 State Vs. Dev Sharma @ Monu & Ors. PS Badarpur Page No. 8 of 48 Sharma @ Monu near around the year 2011 as per Hindu rites and rituals. After marriage of his daughter with accused Dev Sharma she was kept well for about three years. Thereafter, there was some matrimonial disputes between his daughter and devrani and jethani namely Simran and her husband namely Sonu. His daughter used to often asked him on phone as to when he was to sell my land at Bulandshashar and she also told him that she required some money. He told his daughter deceased Sonam that whenever his case which was pending qua the land was resolved, he shall sell the land and give her some money. She used to often call him for aforesaid money and once told him forcefully that she was in urgent need of Rs. Ten Lakhs. Thereafter, his daughter Sonam expired in the year 2014, but he did not remember the date on which she had expired. On the day of her death his wife had received a call from the police station who informed them that his daughter had expired and she has died by hanging. Thereafter, he alongwith his wife and his son namely Raju immediately reached Delhi and straightaway went to the police station. Thereafter, they went to AIIMS Hospital. The postmortem of his daughter was conducted and her dead body was handed over to them on the next day. Thereafter, their statement was recorded before the Tehsildar/Executive Magistrate. Police official were also recorded his statement at police station. His statement was Ex.PW1/A. To his knowledge his daughter used to ask for money from him as she was being pressurized from her matrimonial family. His daughter told him that she was ill-treated by her sister-in-laws namely Simran and another he did not remember. She was ill-treated only by her sister-in- laws and by no other person in her matrimonial family. Jewellery of the deceased was handed over to him and seized by the police vide FIR No.744/2014 State Vs. Dev Sharma @ Monu & Ors. PS Badarpur Page No. 9 of 48 seizure memo Ex.PW1/B. His statement was recorded by IO regarding identity of the dead body which was Ex.PW1/C. He had received the dead body of his deceased daughter vide receipt Ex.PW1/D. During cross examination PW1 deposed that his deceased daughter Sonam had solemnized court marriage with the accused Dev Sharma @ Monu and he did not know the place where they had solemnized their marriage and the exact date when she got married with accused Dev Sharma @ Monu. It was correct that neither he nor his family members had participated in the marriage of his deceased daughter Sonam with accused Dev Sharma @ Monu. It was correct that he had not given any dowry in the marriage of his deceased daughter Sonam. It was correct that it was a love marriage between his decease daughter and accused Dev Sharma @ Monu. It was correct that his daughter had left the parental home 4-5 days prior to her marriage with accused Dev Sharma @ Monu. It was correct that after marriage with accused Dev Sharma @ Monu she returned back to the parental home at Tajpur Pahadi, Badarpur, Delhi. The distance between his house of Tajpur Pahadi, and accused Dev Sharma @ Monu was about 500 meter away. He had not filed any police compliant when his daughter Sonam left the house. It was correct that his deceased daughter Sonam after her marriage with accused Dev Sharma @ Monu stayed at her matrimonial house situated at D-1305, Tajpur Pahadi, Near Barat Ghar, Badarpur, Delhi. It was correct that he had left his house of Tajpur Pahadi after one year and shifted back to his village due to the disrespect in the society due to the marriage of his daughter Sonam with accused Dev Sharma @ Monu. It was correct FIR No.744/2014 State Vs. Dev Sharma @ Monu & Ors. PS Badarpur Page No. 10 of 48 that his son Raj Kumar continued stay at Tajpur Pahadi. He did not have any relatives who are residing in the area of Tajpur Pahadi. His daughter deceased Sonam visited him in his village at Sikandarabad, Bulandshashar, UP after two years of her marriage. He had stayed at Tajpur Pahadi, for about 16-17 years prior to shifting to his village. It was correct that he had cordial relation with the people in his neighborhood of Tajpur Pahadi while he stayed there. He did not know the date of birth of his deceased daughter Sonam. Sonam was blessed with two children but he did not know the place of their birth or their date of birth. It was correct that both the children have been residing with accused Dev Sharma @ Monu since there birth. It was correct that his daughter Sonam always stayed at her matrimonial house. His daughter had visited him only once in the village after her marriage and he did not remember the exact date month, or year when she visited him. His daughter and he had never filed any complaint against the behaviour of the accused persons to any police authority at Sikendarabad. He and his daughter deceased Sonam had never filed any complaint to any police authority in Delhi or in UP against the accused persons or their behaviour regarding beatings given to his daughter or their demand of Rs. Ten Lakhs as a dowry. He did not remember if he had given his mobile number or his daughter mobile number to the IO or the Tehsildar/Executive Magistrate during investigation of the present matter. He did not know if his daughter had made any 100 number call or given any complaint in the police station at Badarpur regarding misbehavior and beatings by the accused persons or any demand of dowry. His daughter namely Radha was younger to his daughter Sonam. It was correct that his younger daughter Radha had solemnized love marriage with Jai Dev Sharma FIR No.744/2014 State Vs. Dev Sharma @ Monu & Ors. PS Badarpur Page No. 11 of 48 who was the real younger brother of accused Dev Sharma @ Monu. It was correct that the aforesaid marriage was solemnized between his daughter Radha and Jai Dev Sharma after about 2-3 years after the death of his daughter Sonam. It was correct that neither he nor his family members had participated in the marriage between his daughter Radha and Jai Dev Sharma. It was correct that he had not given any dowry in the marriage of his daughter Radha with Jai Dev Sharma. It was correct that his daughter Radha was blessed with one daughter who was currently around seven years of age. His daughter Radha and Jai Dev Sharma have been residing the aforesaid house only for past one year and prior to that they were living separately. It was correct that he had informed his other family members regarding whatever his deceased daughter Sonam used to share with him. His daughter Radha had been married for about 8½ years now. It was correct that his daughter Radha has not filed any police complaint against the accused persons during the aforesaid 8½ years. It was correct that accused Dev Sharma @ Monu had visited his house at his village and attended several functions even after the demise of his daughter Sonam. After the dead body of his daughter was given to them, her cremation was performed at Delhi. After the demise of his daughter he had stayed in Delhi for about 8-9 days at the house of Tajpur Pahadi with his son.

He did not remember the exact time when his statement was recorded by Tehsildar/Executive Magistrate, but the same was recorded around afternoon. To his knowledge, his statement was recorded by the police prior to the statement recorded by Tehsildar/Executive Magistrate. It was correct that his other family members and relatives were present there when his statement was recorded by the Tehsildar/Executive Magistrate. He did not remember if he was served with any notice by FIR No.744/2014 State Vs. Dev Sharma @ Monu & Ors. PS Badarpur Page No. 12 of 48 the police officials on 27.12.2014, to furnish the documents pertaining to the land mentioned by him at his village in the statement to the concerned Tehsildar/ Executive Magistrate. Witness was shown one notice U/s 91 Cr.P.C. dated 27.12.2014, and the same was Ex. PW1/D1. He had not handed over any document pertaining to his property or the pending case regarding his property to the IO during investigation of the present matter. It was correct that he had told his daughter Sonam that his younger daughter Radha should not solemnized marriage with Jai Dev Sharma. It was correct that he had not given any dowry to my daughters Sonam and Radha in their marriage or after their marriage.

PW-2 Smt. Omwati (mother of the deceased) deposed that deceased Sonam was her daughter and she got married with the accused Dev Sharma @ Monu in the month of January, 2011. Initially, her daughter was residing happily with the accused persons. Thereafter, the quarrel took place between her daughter and her in-laws. The in- laws used to pressurize her daughter to go out from their home and in- laws of her daughter used to pressurized her daughter to bring money from them. They have tried to make her understand. Quarrel used to take place between husband and wife. On 18.12.2014, she received a phone from police official that her daughter had hanged herself. They immediately reached at her house. Police officials were also present there and they removed the dead body from the fan and dead body of her daughter was lying on the bed. Police immediately had taken dead body of her daughter to the Safdarganj Hospital. They had suspicious on the incident that her daughter hanged herself and there was no possibility to hang herself because there was small height of the bed FIR No.744/2014 State Vs. Dev Sharma @ Monu & Ors. PS Badarpur Page No. 13 of 48 and fan and her daughter never commit suicide. They suspected that accused persons hanged her daughter after committing her murder and she was hanged by the in-laws to show that her daughter hanging herself. When they reached at the in-laws house of her daughter, nobody from her in-law family were present at the spot and only police official were present at the spot.

During cross-examination PW-2 deposed that her statement was recorded on the next date of the death of her daughter by the police officials around 12 noon. Her statement was read over to her by the police officials. She had informed the police officials regarding the fact that her daughter was found hanging from the fan and the distance between the fan and the bed was not much and it could not have been possible for her to have died due to hanging. It was correct that neither she nor her family members or any relatives had attended the wedding of her deceased daughter with accused Dev Sharma @ Monu. She did not know the date of marriage of her daughter or the place where she solemnized her marriage since she did not attend the same. It was correct that his daughter deceased Sonam had love marriage with accused Dev Sharma. It was correct that his daughter got married with accused Dev Sharma without her consent and knowledge. After the marriage of her daughter she alongwith her family stayed at the house of Taj Pur Pahadi only for a year and thereafter, they all shifted to their native village. It was correct that during their stay at Taj Pur Pahadi both Sonam and Dev Sharma used to visit at their house. After the marriage of Sonam and Dev Sharma she used to visit at the matrimonial house of the Sonam but PW2, her husband and her son never visited at the matrimonial house of her daughter. During their FIR No.744/2014 State Vs. Dev Sharma @ Monu & Ors. PS Badarpur Page No. 14 of 48 stay at Taj Pur Pahadi Badarpur New Delhi, they did not make any written complaint against accused persons for cruelty, harassment or demand of dowry to police. After the marriage, her daughter first time came at their house at Taj Pur Pahadi after 2-3 months of her marriage. Her daughter Radha got married after one year of the death of her daughter Sonam. It was correct that marriage of her daughter Radha was also a love marriage. It was correct that neither she nor her family members or relatives had attended the marriage of her daughter Radha and the same was performed without her consent and knowledge. It was correct that they had not given any complaint to any police authority or officer before the death of her daughter Sonam regarding the cruelties upon her. It was correct that since the marriage of her deceased daughter Sonam which was solemnized by her without the consent of herself and her family members initially they were not happy with the same. She had visited the matrimonial house of her deceased daughter Sonam even after shifting to the native village. It was correct that accused Dev Sharma alongwith his children had visited her house to attend a family function. She had informed the police during investigation the phone number of her deceased daughter Sonam and her phone number. She did not know if her deceased daughter Sonam used to talk to her younger daughter Radha on phone. When her daughter Sonam had visited at their native village she had stayed for one week and during her stay, she used to talk to her younger daughter Radha. She did not know if her deceased daughter Sonam or her daughter Radha had ever made any complaint to police or made a call at 100 number to inform regarding the cruelties upon her by the accused persons. She did not know if her daughter had made any complaint to the police in the first year of her FIR No.744/2014 State Vs. Dev Sharma @ Monu & Ors. PS Badarpur Page No. 15 of 48 marriage when they were also residing at Tajpur Pahadi, Delhi. She had received the call from the police officials regarding the demise of her daughter. They had reached Delhi from their native village within 2 hours of receiving the aforesaid information. When they had received Delhi and went to the matrimonial house of her deceased daughter Sonam they found that several public persons have gathered at the spot. They remained at the matrimonial house for about 20-25 minutes, and thereafter, went to AIIMS Hospital. Police officials did not record their statement at that time. Police did not record the statement of any public person on the spot in her presence.

PW-3 Raj Kumar (brother of the deceased) deposed that his deceased sister had love marriage with Dev Sharma @ Monu in the month of January, 2011. She was living with accused Dev Sharma @ Monu in the area of Tajpur Pahadi, Delhi. She used to talk with his mother as her in-laws harassed her and she stated that her mother-in-law, jethani, jeth and her husband used to torture her mentally and physically and demand money from her. She was pressurized by her in-laws that she will have to arrange money for them and given to her in-laws. His mother had conveyed to his father regarding the demand of in-laws of his sister. His father stated to his mother that whenever their land would be sold then they could arrange money for in-laws of his sister. She never discussed about the demand of money from him. She used to discuss with his parents to arrange the money of Rs.10 Lakh as per demand of in-laws. Their land could not be sold and accused persons continuously tortured his sister. On 18.12.2014, some police officials informed his mother that his sister had hanged herself. When his mother had called his sister but she did not responded. Thereafter, FIR No.744/2014 State Vs. Dev Sharma @ Monu & Ors. PS Badarpur Page No. 16 of 48 they immediately reached at the house of his sister. The family of in- laws of his sister were not present there. The police officials were not present at the spot. He went to the police station. On 19.12.2014, they informed by the police official that he should go to mortuary because his sister had expired. They received the dead body from mortuary of his deceased sister after postmortem. He did not remember whether any jewellery article worn by his sister at the time of her death but the some were removed from her dead body and handed over to his father. He had signed the memo of receiving the jewellery/articles Ex.PW1/B. During cross-examination PW-3 deposed that it was correct that on the day of demise of his sister Sonam he was residing at D-74 Budh Vihar, Tajpur Pahadi, Badarpur, Delhi. PW3 resided at the address of Tajpur Pahadi, Delhi for about two and half years from the year 2009- 2011. His family members including his parents, his wife, his children and his one sister used to reside in the aforesaid house but in separate portions. After the marriage of his sister Sonam his parents and his younger sister Radha left the aforesaid house and shifted to native village after two months of the marriage of his sister Sonam. It was correct that both his sisters i.e. deceased Sonam and his sister Radha solemnized their marriages without their consent and knowledge. It was correct that he did not participate or attended the marriage of both his sisters and therefore, he did not know the day or place where they got married. His sister Sonam never visited his aforesaid house after her marriage. It was correct that his family members were upset due to the marriage performed by deceased Sonam without the consent or knowledge of his family members. It was correct that due to the FIR No.744/2014 State Vs. Dev Sharma @ Monu & Ors. PS Badarpur Page No. 17 of 48 aforesaid marriage performed by his deceased sister Sonam there was disrespect in the society and vicinity. He never used to speak to his deceased sister Sonam on phone. The distance between his aforesaid house of Tajpur Pahadi and the house of accused persons was at the distance of 10 minutes by walking. The distance between of his aforesaid house and PS Badarpur was about 15-20 minutes by walking. He did not know if his sister deceased Sonam had ever made 100 number call or gave written complaint against accused persons at PS Badarpur. He came to know within six months of the marriage of his deceased sister Sonam that accused persons had demanded Rs.10 Lakhs from them. They came to know about the aforesaid fact regarding demand of dowry from his sister by the accused persons within six months of her marriage. He have never filed any written complaint at PS Badarpur or in their native village at UP against the accused persons regarding demand of dowry. He never told about the fact of demand of dowry to any neighbor or relatives. His younger sister Radha was married to younger brother of accused Dev Sharma almost after 4-6 months of the demised of his sister Sonam. He did not know the date of their marriage. Police officials never visited his house at Tajpur Pahadi to enquire about the present matter. He did not know if any police official visited his native village to enquiry about the present matter. He did not know if his statement was recorded by the SDM concerned but his statement was recorded only once in the present matter by the police official. Police had not recorded any statement of witness in his presence.

PW-4 Inspt. B.D. Meena deposed that on 18.12.2014 he was posted as SI at PS Badarpur and received information through DD No.47A FIR No.744/2014 State Vs. Dev Sharma @ Monu & Ors. PS Badarpur Page No. 18 of 48 which was Ex. A-2 regarding hanging by one victim namely Sonam. Upon receiving the said information, he had reached the spot i.e. H.No.D-1305, 1st Floor Near Barat Ghar, Tajpur Pahadi, Delhi. Thereafter, when he reached at the spot, he found that several public persons had gathered on the spot and he found that the aforesaid victim namely Sonam was hanging from the fan by one chunni in a room which was adjacent to the kitchen. He also found that the latch of the room was broken from inside. Thereafter, he informed the crime team who reached at the spot. The crime team took photograph of the spot and prepared the crime report. The photographs of deceased Sonam in hanging position and report was Ex. A-3 (Colly). Upon inquiry he came to know that deceased Sonam had expired within 7 years of marriage, and therefore, he informed the same to SDM Sarita Vihar. He directed him to preserve dead body at AIIMS Mortuary and also to inform the family of the deceased. THE LAW

22.I am firstly dealing with the offences of Section 498A IPC.

23.Here, I must mention relevant law with respect to Section 498A IPC.

24.Section 498A IPC mandates that a husband or relative of the husband of a woman, who subjects a woman to cruelty, shall be punished with a term which may extent to three years and fine. Explanation to the said provision gives meaning to "cruelty" in following manner.

a) any willful conduct which is of such a nature as is likely to drive the woman to commit suicide or to cause grave injury or danger to life, limb or health (whether mental or physical) of the woman; or

b) harassment of the woman where such harassment is with a view to coercing her or any person related to her to meet any unlawful demand for any property or valuable security or is on account of demand for any property or valuable security or is on account of failure by her or any person related to her to meet such demand.

25.Cruelty, therefore, can be either mental or physical. It is difficult to strait jacket the term cruelty by means of a definition because cruelty is a relative term. What constitutes cruelty for one may not constitute cruelty for another person. Reliance in this regard is placed upon case FIR No.744/2014 State Vs. Dev Sharma @ Monu & Ors. PS Badarpur Page No. 37 of 48 law titled as G.V. Siddara Ramesh Versus Statement of Karnatka (2010) 3SCC 152.

26.Further, Section 498A IPC was added with a view to punishing husband and his relatives, who harass or tortured the wife to coerce her or her relatives to satisfy unlawful demands of dowry. The hyper technical view would be counter productive and would act against the interest of women and against the object for which provision was added. Reliance in this regard is placed upon case titled as B.S. Joshi Versus State of Haryana, AIR 2003 SC 1386.

27.After considering above provision and interpretation of the same by Hon'ble Apex Court, I find that above provision was made by legislature, to safeguard the interest of a married woman who is subjected to mental or physical cruelty by her husband or relatives of husband. The said cruelty could lead that woman to commit suicide or to cause grave injury to her life, limb or health, which can be either physical or mental. That cruelty also could be based on harassment done to her for getting dowry from her. Based on said understanding of law, I am proceeding further and appreciating facts and evidence of this case.

28.Further, Section 304B IPC states as below Section 304B, IPC, Dowry Death (1) Where the death of a woman is caused by any burns or bodily injury or occurs otherwise than under normal circumstances within seven years of her marriage and it is shown that soon before her FIR No.744/2014 State Vs. Dev Sharma @ Monu & Ors. PS Badarpur Page No. 38 of 48 death. she was subjected to cruelty or harassment by her husband or any relative of her husband for, or in connection with, any demand for dowry, such death shall be called "Dowry death", and such husband or relative shall be deemed to have caused her death. Explanation: For the purpose of this sub-section "dowry" shall have the same meaning as in S.2 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 (28 of 1961).

(2) Whoever commits dowry death shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than seven years but which may extend to imprisonment for life."

29.The necessity for insertion of the aforesaid provision was keeping in view the impediment in the pre-existing laws in securing evidence to prove dowry related deaths. The legislature thought it wise to insert a provision relating to presumption of dowry death (Section 113 B of Indian Evidence Death, 1872) on proof of certain essentials. The three ingredients for establishing the offence U/s 304B IPC are

a) that there is a demand of dowry and harassment by the accused.

b) that the deceased died

c) that the death is under unnatural circumstances.

30.Therefore, once there is harassment for the payment of dowry and unnatural death occurred within seven years after the marriage, the presumption of dowry death is inherent. Further, it has also been stated that the death of a woman is either by burns or bodily injury or otherwise then under normal circumstances, and should be within FIR No.744/2014 State Vs. Dev Sharma @ Monu & Ors. PS Badarpur Page No. 39 of 48 seven years of marriage and it should also be shown that soon before her death she was subjected to cruelty or harassment by husband or relative of her husband and such harassment or cruelty should pertain to demand of dowry.

31.The aforesaid offence shall apply whenever the occurrence of death is preceded by cruelty or harassment by husband or in-laws for dowry and death occurs in unnatural circumstances. The intention behind the section is to fasten guilt on the husband or in-laws though they did not infact caused the death.

32. As to the origin of dowry or dos primarily was a contribution by the wife's family or by the wife herself intended to assist the husband in bearing the expenses of conjugal household. The genesis of dowry was understood as a social set up and soon dowry became a social evil in the society. It is an offence brutal and barbaric. It is generally committed inside the house and more often with the circumstance to given an impression that it was a suicidal death. Often the perpetrator of crime attempt to cover up such offence by giving it a color of suicide. However, section 113A of the Indian Evidence Act raises presumption of cruelty as defined U/s 498A IPC against the husband or his relative if the wife commits suicide within a period fo seven years from the date of her marriage. Therefore, the section provides that such husband or relative shall be deemed to have caused her death and shall be punished with imprisonment for maximum of seven years but which may extent to life imprisonment. Importantly, section 304B of the IPC does not categorized death as homicidal, or suicidal or accidental. This is because the death caused by burns can, in a given FIR No.744/2014 State Vs. Dev Sharma @ Monu & Ors. PS Badarpur Page No. 40 of 48 case, be homicidal or suicidal or accidental. The aforesaid provision was inserted with a view to combat the increasing menace of dowry deaths in India. Section 113B of Indian Evidence Act says that when the question is whether a person has committed a dowry death of a woman, and it is shown that soon before her death such woman had been subjected by such person to cruelty or harassment for or in connection with any demand for dowry, the court shall presume that such person had caused dowry death. Therefore, the death by suicidal hanging also is encompassed by the section. For the purposes of this section "dowry" shall have the same meaning as in section 2 of the dowry prohibition act 1961. "Dowry" means any property or valuable security given or agreed to be given either directly or indirectly, a) by one party to a marriage to the other party to the marriage, or b) by the parents of either party to a marriage or by any other person, to either party to the marriage or to any other person, at or before or any time, after the marriage in connection with the marriage of the said parties, but does not include dower or in the case of persons to whom the Muslim Personal Law applies.

33.Further, Section 304B and Section 498A are not mutually exclusive. The provisions deal with two distinct offences. It is true that " cruelty"

is a common essential to both the section and that has to be proved. The explanation of section 498A gives the meaning of cruelty. In Section 304B there is no such explanation about the meaning of cruelty but having regard to the common back ground to these offences, the meaning of "cruelty of harassment" will be the same as given in explanation to Section 498A under which " cruelty" by itself amounts to an offence and its punishable. U/s 304B it is the dowry FIR No.744/2014 State Vs. Dev Sharma @ Monu & Ors. PS Badarpur Page No. 41 of 48 death that is punishable and such death should be occurred within seven years of marriage. However, no such period is mentioned in section 498A and the husband or his relatives would be liable for subjecting the woman to cruelty and time after the marriage.

34.To attract the provision of section 304B of the IPC one of the main ingredients of the offence which is required to be established is that "soon before her death" she was subjected to cruelty and harassment "in connection with demand of dowry". The expression "soon before her death" cannot be given a restricted or a narrower meaning. It must be understood in their plain language and with reference to their meaning in common parlance. These are the provisions relating to human behaviour and therefore cannot be given such a narrower meaning, which would defeat the very purpose of the provision of the act. The legislative object in providing such a radius of time by employing the words soon before her death" is to emphasize the idea that her death should, in all probability, has been the aftermath of such cruelty or harassment. In other words there should be a reasonable, if not direct, nexus between her death and the dowry related cruelty or harassment inflicted upon her. However, the said expression would normally imply that the inverter should not be much between the concerned cruelty or harassment and the death in question. If the alleged incident of cruelty is remote in time and has became stale enough not to disturb the mental equilibrium of the woman concerned, it would be of no consequence. Further, it has been held in " Rajinder Singh Vs. State of Punjab" 2015 Crl. J. 1934 that "soon before" is not synonymous with "immediately before".

FIR No.744/2014 State Vs. Dev Sharma @ Monu & Ors. PS Badarpur Page No. 42 of 48

35.The word "dowry demand", demand neither conceived nor would conceived of any agreement. Section 304B refers to demand of dowry, it refers to demand of property of valuable security as referred to the definition fo dowry under the act.

APPRECIATION OF EVIDENCE

36.As per the prosecution story, PW-1 Sh. Sunil Kumar being the father of the deceased had lodged complaint with police, Ex.PW1/A in which he had claimed that accused persons were demanding dowry from their deceased daughter namely Sonam who had married accused Dev Sharma @ Monu. Further, so, based on said claims, it was clear that deceased Sonam, as per prosecution story had committed suicide on account of the fact that she was harassed by accused persons to bring dowry. Further, that on several occasions his daughter had spoken to him on the phone and used to inquire from him regarding his land dispute and also that she was in need of Rs.10 Lakh. Further, that the deceased had got married with accused no.1 without their consent and that PW1 and his family members had not attended the marriage of the deceased and he was not knowing the date or place when the deceased got married to accused no.1. On the other hand PW2 Smt. Omwati being the mother of the deceased has deposed that the deceased got married to accused no.1 in January, 2011 and her daughter was residing happily with accused persons initially but later on there were some quarrels between the deceased and her inlaws and the in-laws of the deceased used to pressurize her daughter to leave the matrimonial house and also to bring money from PW1 and PW2. She has also deposed that her daughter had visited them after one week of her marriage. On the other hand PW1 has FIR No.744/2014 State Vs. Dev Sharma @ Monu & Ors. PS Badarpur Page No. 43 of 48 stated that after the marriage of the deceased with accused no.1 she was kept well by accused persons for three years i.e. from 2011 till 2014 and only thereafter, some matrimonial disputes between the his deceased daughter and Devrani and Jethani of the deceased had taken place. PW1 did not deposed on the line of his complaint and therefore, was cross examined by the prosecution.

37.In the present matter, during cross examination PW1 and PW2 have admitted during their cross examination that none of them had attended the marriage of deceased as she had got married to accused no.1 without their consent. Both the aforesaid witnesses admitted that they had never given any dowry in the marriage of their deceased daughter since it was a love marriage and that the deceased had left her parental home 4-5 days prior to her marriage with accused. They have also admitted that after the marriage of deceased with accused No.1 Dev Sharma @ Monu they had left their house in Delhi situated at Tajpur Pahadi, Badarpur and PW1 and PW2 alongwith their daughter shifted to their native village and it was only their son that is PW3 Raj Kumar continued to stay at the house of Tajpur Pahadi, Delhi. Both the witnesses PW1 and PW2 admitted that their daughter Radha had solemnized marriage with the younger brother of accused Dev Sharma @ Monu soon after the demise of deceased Sonam, and the same was also a love marriage and they had not given any dowry in the marriage of their daughter Radha also. Both witnesses PW1 & PW2 admitted that accused no.1 even after the demise of their deceased daughter Sonam had been visiting them in their native village and have attended functions of the family. PW3 who is the brother of deceased has on the contradictory stated that the accused FIR No.744/2014 State Vs. Dev Sharma @ Monu & Ors. PS Badarpur Page No. 44 of 48 persons had started harassing the deceased and tortured her mentally and physically and demanded dowry from the deceased soon after the marriage. The aforesaid fact was conveyed by the deceased to PW2 who had informed the same to PW1. However, PW1 and PW2 have not stated so in their testimonies recorded before the Court. Further PW3 had stated that the demand of dowry were never told by the deceased to PW3 as he hardly had spoken to her after her marriage and was not in touch with the deceased. PW3 has stated that he had heard from his parents about the aforesaid fact and that deceased Sonam had asked his parents to arrange Rs.10 Lakh as the same was demanded by the in-laws of the deceased. However, even the aforesaid fact is not stated by PW1 and PW2 in their testimonies. The aforesaid statement of PW3 can only be termed as hear say in nature and more so the averments made by PW3 are not supported by PW1 and PW2. PW3 during his cross examination has stated that both his sisters deceased Sonam and Radha had solemnized their marriages without their consent and knowledge and that PW3 had not participated or attended the marriage of both his sisters. PW3 further deposed that deceased Sonam never visited their house after her marriage, and that due to the aforesaid fact of solemnizing the marriage by the deceased Sonam have brought disrespect in the society and therefore, PW3 had never spoken to the deceased on phone and it was only PW2 (mother of the deceased) who used to speak to deceased Sonam. All the three witnesses i.e. PW1, PW2 and PW3 have stated that neither of them, nor the deceased had ever made any 100 number call or had given any written complaint against the accused persons for demand of dowry or the harassment towards dowry. Further, that none of the witnesses has stated that upon hearing FIR No.744/2014 State Vs. Dev Sharma @ Monu & Ors. PS Badarpur Page No. 45 of 48 regarding the harassment to the deceased, they had filed any complaint in their native village or in Delhi against the accused persons prior to the death of deceased Sonam.

38.PW1 Sunil Kumar, PW2 Smt. Omwati and PW3 Raj Kumar being the family members of the deceased did not depose regarding any incident to infer that the accused persons had committed any kind of cruelty or harassment upon the deceased while she was living in the matrimonial house or any kind of cruelty or harassment with demand of dowry from the side of accused persons soon before her death. None of the witnesses examined by prosecution stated that deceased Sonam faced cruelty of any form, at the hands of accused persons.

39.Further, PW3 Raj Kumar being the brother of deceased Sonam also did not depose that accused had committed any cruelty or harassment on her sister, immediately prior to her death. Further, PW1 and PW2 being the parents of the deceased also stated that the deceased Sonam was kept well in her matrimonial home by the accused persons for three years after her marriage. So, their evidence also did not prove the aspect of cruelty faced by deceased Sonam at the hands of accused persons.

40. Further it has been argued on behalf of Ld. Counsel for accused persons that witness namely Hem Raj Sharma who was examined as witness by the concerned SDM and was the neighbourer of the accused persons also deposed that the deceased was never subjected to cruelty, however, the aforesaid witness was not cited as a prosecution witness by the IO, for the reasons best known to him.

FIR No.744/2014 State Vs. Dev Sharma @ Monu & Ors. PS Badarpur Page No. 46 of 48

41.PW4 Inspt B D Meena, PW6 Inspt. Rajesh Kumar, PW7 Inspt. Satish Chandra, PW8 Ms. Riya from FSL and PW9 SI Abhay Raj were the formal witnesses being the the IO and FSL examiner of the present matter, deposed regarding the manner of investigation conducted. Further, the FSL report regarding the data retrieved from the mobile phone of the deceased also do not show that there were any communication with the family of the deceased to ascertain that she was subjected to cruelty. Further, the FSL report pertaining to viscera also shows on chemical, microscopic, TLC, and GC - HS examination, metallic poisons ethyl and methyl alcohol, cyanide, phosphide, alkaloids, barbiturates, tranquilizers, and pesticides could not be detected in Ex.1A, Ex.1B, Ex.1C & Ex.1D . Further, the postmortem report of the deceased which was Ex.A4, has opined the cause of death as asphyxia due to ante-mortem hanging, viscera has been kept to rule out concomitant intoxication. Further, in the column of injuries upon the dead body of the deceased it has been mentioned ligature mark of width 2.5 cm at the anterior aspect of middle neck. Further, there were no injuries found on head, chest, abdomen, or any other part of the body.

42.Further the deceased did not leave any suicide note which could infer that she was subjected to cruelty. All the other witnesses examined by the prosecution did not deposed regarding any of the incident by which it could be inferred that the deceased was subjected to any kind of dowry demand and the averments made on behalf of the family members of the deceased regarding demand of Rs.10 Lakh is also vague and general in nature and does not inspire confidence. The net FIR No.744/2014 State Vs. Dev Sharma @ Monu & Ors. PS Badarpur Page No. 47 of 48 result is that above mentioned prosecution witnesses, who could have deposed about deceased Sonam facing cruelty or harassment at the hands of accused persons, did not depose so, in their respective testimonies.

43.Rest of the prosecution witnesses were police officials who had done different aspects of investigation. Their unrebutted testimonies, did not prove the aspect of "cruelty" being faced by deceased Sonam, during her lifetime from accused persons. So, I discarded their testimonies.

44.Prosecution thus, failed to prove the essential ingredients of cruelty, constituting the Section 498A/304B/34 IPC.

45.So, prosecution in order to bring conviction of an accused u/sec. 306 IPC has to prove beyond reasonable doubt that accused intended to commit the said offence, by playing active role, thereby abetting victim to commit suicide.

46.Accused persons, per contra, were able to raise defence of them being falsely implicated in this case.

47.Thus, accused persons namely Dev Sharma @ Monu, Sonu, Beermati, and Sonia are acquitted of the offences punishable U/s 498A/304B/34 Digitally signed by SHEETAL IPC. SHEETAL CHAUDHARY CHAUDHARY Date:
